blocks.text: Re: Clearance of a proposed trademark
Dear Ms. Hunter:

Thank you for asking us to advise {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} on whether the name it proposes to adopt can be used and registered as a trademark in the United States for the goods and services it intends to offer under that name. This letter records the work we have agreed to do, the people who will do it, the fee and the date on which the work will begin, and the terms on which we will act for the company, and it becomes our agreement when you countersign it.
Scope

We will advise the company on whether the proposed mark is available for use and for federal registration for the goods and services you have described to us, and, where it is not clearly available, on the nature and extent of the risk that adopting it would carry. If, before we order the full search described below, you ask us to consider an alternative name for the same goods and services, we will include it in this engagement without an additional fee.
How the Work Will Proceed
The work will move through four stages, and each depends on the one before it:

items: Intake. We will confirm with you in writing the mark, the goods and services, the channels through which they will be sold, and any use the company has already made of the name, because every search that follows is run against that description.

Screening search. We will search federal registrations and pending applications for identical and closely similar marks, so that a name with an obvious obstacle can be set aside before the cost of a full search is incurred.

Full search. If the screening search discloses no such obstacle, we will order a full search report covering federal and state registrations, pending applications, business and domain names, and unregistered use in commerce, and we will review each relevant entry against the company's mark.

Memorandum. We will deliver a written clearance memorandum, marked privileged, that assesses the risk of using the mark and the prospects of registering it, identifies the marks on which that assessment rests, and recommends whether the company should proceed, modify the mark, or choose another.

blocks.text: A clearance search speaks as of the date on which it is run. Applications filed and use begun after that date fall outside the memorandum unless you ask us to bring the search up to date, which we would quote for separately.
What This Engagement Does Not Include

The engagement does not include preparing or filing a trademark application, clearance in any country other than the United States, watching the register after the memorandum issues, or representing the company in any opposition, cancellation, demand, or dispute concerning the mark. Where the memorandum suggests that one of those steps deserves your attention it will say so, and any of them would be the subject of a separate letter.
Staffing

I will have overall responsibility for the engagement and will sign the clearance memorandum. Kelly Snyder, an Associate with the firm, will carry out the legal analysis of the search results and will be your usual point of contact, and Ashley Williams, a Patent Agent with the firm, will coordinate the searches, keep a dated record of what was searched and when, and maintain the docket for the matter.

Whether the mark can be used or registered is a legal question, and the conclusions on it will be reached and stated by Ms. Snyder and by me. You should raise with me directly any concern you have about staffing, cost, or the pace of the work.
Fee and Start of Work

Our fee for the work described above is a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.fee}}. Work will begin on {{fact:f:E-2024-001.start}}, provided we have your countersigned copy of this letter by then, and we expect the engagement to run about four months from that date, although the time needed to review the full search depends on how many similar marks it returns and cannot be fixed in advance.

The fixed fee covers the four stages described above and nothing else. The charges of the commercial search provider and any official fees are not part of it; we will bill them at cost, and we will tell you the charge for the full search before we place the order.
Billing and Payment

We will invoice half of the fixed fee when the work begins and the balance when we deliver the memorandum, and we will invoice costs in the month in which they are incurred; each invoice is payable within thirty days of its date. If an invoice remains unpaid sixty days after its date, we may suspend work on written notice to you, and if it remains unpaid thirty days after that notice we may withdraw from the engagement, subject to our obligations under the rules of professional conduct.
Conflicts of Interest

Before sending this letter we checked {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} against our records and found no representation adverse to it. A full search can, however, return a mark owned by a current client of this firm; if it does, we will tell you promptly, we will not advise you on that mark ourselves, and that part of the analysis may need to go to independent counsel.
Term and Termination

This engagement runs from the start date stated above until we have delivered the clearance memorandum and answered your questions on it, and it then ends without further notice unless we agree in writing to continue. Either of us may end it earlier by written notice, in which case the company will owe the part of the fixed fee that corresponds to the work completed by the date of the notice, together with any costs already incurred.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence everything the company gives us in the course of the engagement and will use it only for this work, and until the company adopts the mark we will treat the fact that it is considering the name as confidential, disclosing it only to the search provider and only to the extent the search requires. Our communications with you and the memorandum are intended to be protected by the attorney-client privilege, and to keep that protection we ask that you limit their circulation to the people within the company who need them and speak to us before sharing them with designers, distributors, investors, or anyone else outside it.
Limitation of Liability

A clearance memorandum is a professional judgment based on the search results available when the search is run and on the information the company gives us; it is not a guarantee that no one will object to the mark, that the United States Patent and Trademark Office will register it, or that a court would weigh the risk as we do. No search can find every unregistered use of a name, and we are not responsible for consequences that follow from information that was incomplete or inaccurate when it was given to us. Nothing in this letter limits any liability that the rules of professional conduct do not permit a lawyer to limit in advance.
Governing Law

This letter is governed by the law of the state in which the firm maintains its principal office, without regard to that state's rules on conflicts of law. It is the entire agreement between us on this engagement and may be changed only in a writing signed by both of us.

If these terms are acceptable, please sign below on behalf of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} and return a copy to me. When I have it, Kelly Snyder will send you a written request for the information we need at intake, and the work will begin from your answers.
Sincerely,
What we have to deliver

We owe {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} one written answer. Can it use and register the name it has chosen, and how much risk comes with that choice? Kelly Snyder will write the clearance memorandum, and Mary Bradley will sign it.
The client will want a yes or a no. What we can honestly give is an assessment of risk with its reasons, and the memorandum should be framed that way from the first draft.

The matter opened on {{fact:f:E-2024-001.start}}. Our contact at the client is Cynthia Hunter, the Chief Operating Officer. Every request to the client goes to her in writing, so that we have a record of what we asked and when.
How we have divided the work

items: Intake, Kelly Snyder. Confirm in writing the mark, the goods and services, the sales channels, and any use the client has already made of the name. Every search we run is only as good as this description.

Screening search, Matthew Parrish. Search federal registrations and pending applications for identical and close marks. Anything that looks like an obvious obstacle goes to Kelly before we spend the client's money on a full search.

Full search and review, Kelly Snyder with Matthew Parrish. If screening is clear, we order the full report. Matthew builds the first-pass table of marks, owners, and goods, and Kelly decides which entries need real analysis.
Docket and search log, Ashley Williams. I will docket every client and internal date on the matter. I will also keep a dated log of each search: what was searched, when, and by whom.
Memorandum, Kelly Snyder, reviewed by Mary Bradley. A privileged clearance memorandum with a risk assessment and a recommendation: proceed, modify the mark, or choose another.

blocks.text: One point applies to all of it. Matthew and I are patent agents, and our registration does not extend to trademark matters. We gather, organize, and log the record, while Kelly and Mary draw the conclusions, so nothing we write, internally or to the client, should read as an opinion on the mark.

The fee is fixed, so the scope in the engagement letter is the scope we work to. If the full search returns more than we can review properly in the time we have, Kelly will raise it with Mary early, while there is still room to agree a change with the client.
The coming two weeks

items: Kelly's intake request went to Cynthia Hunter this week. I have docketed the date we asked her to answer by, and I will follow up the day after it if nothing has arrived.
Matthew starts the screening search as soon as the goods description is confirmed. He circulates his table when it is done.
Matthew, please record your search strings in the log as you go. If Kelly needs to rerun or widen a search later, she should be able to see exactly what was done.
Kelly and Mary review that table together before we order the full search. The order is the first real cost to the client, so it needs Mary's approval.
By Monday I will send each of you the docket entries that are yours.

blocks.text: If any assignment here does not match your understanding, please tell me before Matthew begins. I will reissue the list with the change.
Good morning Cynthia,

Both searches are now complete, and we have started working through the results. I am opening this thread so that our updates on the clearance work for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} stay in one place. Kelly and Mary are copied and will add to it as we go.
The screening search showed no obvious obstacle, and with your approval we ordered the full search. Its report came back late last week, and Kelly is now reviewing it entry by entry.
A clear screening result is encouraging, but it is not a conclusion. We will give you our view once Kelly's review is finished, and not before.
Two things from your side would help us finish:

items: A current description of everything you plan to sell under the name, including anything planned for later. The search was run against the description you gave us at the start, and if your plans have grown, we need to know now.
Whether the company has used the name anywhere already, even informally, and if so where and since when.

blocks.text: I have noted the end of next week on our docket for both answers. If either will take longer, a short note to me is all we need.
Regards,
Hi Cynthia,

On the second of Ashley's questions, if the company has used the name at all, please send us the records themselves, not a summary of them: packaging, invoices, price lists, web pages, trade show material, or anything else that shows the name in use, together with the date on which each item was first used or published. If {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} has earlier rights in the name, how strong they are will depend on what those records show, and a date that rests on recollection alone is difficult to rely on if it is ever challenged.

Until we have given you our written view, I would also ask that the company not commit to printed packaging, signage, or a public announcement under the name. None of those steps would be decisive on its own, but each one adds to the cost of changing course if the review turns up a mark that we cannot advise you to proceed against.
If a short call would be easier than putting all of this in writing, please tell Kelly which days this week suit you, and she will set one up.
Sincerely,
Good morning Cynthia,
Copies are all we need for the records Mary described. Scans or photographs taken on a phone are fine, and the originals should stay in the company's files where they are now.

Please send items to me as they turn up, without waiting to gather everything first. I log each one against the matter with the date it reached us, so nothing goes missing between our office and Kelly's review.
If any use took place outside the United States, a note of the country will do for now. We will come back to you if it bears on the review of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}'s mark.
Kelly is still glad to take the call Mary mentioned, if you would rather walk through what you have before sending it.
Regards,
Hi Cynthia,

One addition to Ashley's note, which I should have made in my own: the copies should be of records as they were kept at the time, and nothing should be recreated, retyped, or updated now, even where a newer version would be easier to read. A document prepared after the fact carries little weight if the date of first use is ever questioned, and an original with a visible date, however rough it looks, is worth more to {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} than a clean version without one.
Nothing else in our plan changes, and the end of next week remains the date we are working to for both of Ashley's questions.
Once Kelly has the records and the updated product description, she will complete her review of the full search, and I will then write to you to arrange a time to go through our conclusions together.
Sincerely,
